Hi Emily - quick technical note from Security/Platform about the questions you raised. TL;DR: SOC 2 Type II available on request; BAA is supported but only for Dedicated and Private deployment modes. Hosted multi-tenant API is not eligible for BAA. Details below.

SOC / Compliance:
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (Security, Availability, Confidentiality) - redacted report available on request: https://redwood.app/oss/soc2/HC-redacted-2029.pdf
- We have GDPR controls in place: data processing agreements, data subject request flows, and regional data residency options for Private deployments.

HIPAA / BAA specifics:
- BAA availability: Redwood will sign a BAA for customers using Redwood Dedicated (reserved, single-tenant GPU pools) and Redwood Private (VPC or on-premises). We do not sign BAAs for our shared, hosted multi-tenant API.
- Rationale: Dedicated/Private provide the necessary tenant isolation, customer-controlled networking, and audit segregation required in BAAs. Our hosted service is architected for low-latency multi-tenant access and cannot meet the contractual isolation guarantees a BAA requires.

PHI handling boundaries and recommendations:
- Allowed under BAA-eligible modes (Dedicated/Private): patient identifiers, clinical notes, diagnostic codes, images (if provisioned in Private), etc., subject to your internal policies and retention rules.
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): recommended for non-PHI or de-identified data only (tokenized or hashed identifiers; no direct identifiers).
- Encryption: data in transit is TLS 1.3; at-rest encryption with customer KMS options for Dedicated/Private. HSM integrations available for Private deployments.
- Audit & logging: per-request audit logs and token-level tracing available in Dedicated/Private; logs can be exported to your SIEM (Syslog/S3) under contract.

Operational constraints:
- Data residency: Private deployments can be provisioned in a customer VPC/region; Dedicated has region selection but is still managed infrastructure. If strict residency is required, Private on-prem is recommended.
- Onboarding timeline: Dedicated ~6-8 weeks from contract signature (in region availability permitting); Private on-prem variable depending on install window and network scheduling.

Next steps we suggest:
1) HealthCloud Security to complete the attached vendor questionnaire (we've filled common answers where applicable).
2) We can provide a redacted SOC 2 report and standard BAA template for initial review - see link above.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra team to validate network/ingress patterns and retention settings (Vivek, can you propose 2x 30m slots?).

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Redacted.pdf (redacted report), Vendor questionnaire (already attached to thread)

If you want, I can also loop in our legal lead to discuss any specific BAA clauses your counsel requires.

--
